correctness.rationale: The second-coordinate period-two condition gives opposite first coordinates ±u, and the first-coordinate equations imply |v|+|v+u|=ell_beta=2(1-1/beta). Its exact shifted modulus identity partitions all real candidate pairs into positive, negative, and crossing sign branches, including boundary identifications. Monotone scalar cosine equations yield unique roots and exact A± branch domains; at ell_beta=pi/2 the crossing equation fixes the locked orbit independent of alpha. Taylor expansion gives pole coefficient pi² beta_c³/16. Direct two-step Jacobian products and Jury/Schur inequalities yield the strict smooth crossing sink criterion and expanding positive-ordinate multiplier, excluding nonsmooth zero ordinates. Independently evaluated sample returns and locked pair corroborate but do not prove exhaustion.

final_claim: For alpha,beta>0 map F(x,y)=(alpha cos x+beta(|y|-1)x,y+x) on full R², all prime-two orbits are classified: none beta≤1; below beta_c=4/(4-pi), two/one/zero as alpha crosses A_+(beta); at/above beta_c, exactly two for all alpha, including a beta_c locked orbit independent alpha. A_± have explicit pole and smooth crossing two-cycle has sharp Schur sink iff 1<beta<2 and alpha below both geometric and multiplier thresholds.
limitations: Only strict prime period two and smooth sign-crossing linear sinks; no longer-period orbits, global attraction, bifurcation at nonsmooth boundaries, or hardware claims.
